B1: Computational Thinking

SL: 5 hours | HL: 5 hours

Unit Overview

In this unit, you learn how to define problems clearly and how to approach them in a computational way. This unit underpins the whole course and helps you think like a computer scientist, not just write code.

Unit Objectives

What students are expected to know:

  • how to write a clear problem specification
  • the core ideas of computational thinking, including abstraction, decomposition, pattern recognition and algorithmic design
  • how computational thinking is used to solve real problems
  • how to read and trace flowcharts

Unit Outcomes

What students are expected to be able to do:

  • construct a problem specification
  • describe the fundamental concepts of computational thinking
  • explain how computational thinking is used to solve problems
  • trace flowcharts for a range of algorithms

Subtopics

B1.1

Approaches to computational thinking — problem specification, core computational-thinking concepts, problem-solving strategies and flowcharts

 B1.2

Computational thinking — abstraction, decomposition, pattern recognition

 B1.3

Flowcharts and pseudocode — reading, tracing and constructing flowcharts

 B1.4

Algorithm design — designing step-by-step solutions to problems
